source_refs.note: 5. Plastic and Solid Waste: a main subheading of 33.3 Common Water Pollutants, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 250-254.

blocks.text: Plastic and solid waste pollution in oceans and other water bodies is a growing environmental crisis. Millions of tons of plastic waste including bottles, bags, fishing nets, and microplastics are dumped into rivers, lakes, and oceans every year. Unlike organic materials, plastics do not biodegrade; instead, they break down into smaller particles that persist in the environment for centuries.

Marine animals often mistake plastic for food, leading to ingestion, choking, or internal injury, which can be fatal. Sometimes entanglement in old fishing gear and other debris in the sea bed also causes injury or death to countless sea creatures, including turtles, dolphins, and birds. Furthermore, microplastics have entered the food chain, raising concerns about their impact on human health. Solid waste pollution also clogs waterways, disrupts aquatic habitats, and reduces water quality.

blocks.prompt: i. Name the sources of heavy metals.
blocks.explanation: Industrial wastewater, mining and improper disposal of waste. Mercury: burning coal, gold mining, thermometer and battery factories. Lead: leaded petrol, lead pipes, lead-acid batteries, paints. Cadmium: metal plating, plastic stabilisers, impurities in phosphate fertilizers.

blocks.prompt: ii. How oil spill is hazardous to the marine life?
blocks.explanation: An oil layer blocks sunlight and reduces oxygen exchange; mammals swallow the toxic oil while grooming; fish suffer long-term harm from the hydrocarbons; mangroves, coral reefs and beaches are damaged.

blocks.prompt: iii. Pesticides like DDT are “non-polar and insoluble in water” yet they “pollute water and cause severe human health issues. Explain.
blocks.explanation: A very small amount of DDT does dissolve in water, and it also reaches water attached to soil particles in runoff. It is fat-soluble and persistent, so it builds up in the fatty tissues of fish and increases at each step of the food chain (biomagnification). In this way top predators and humans take in large amounts.
